day1_pitch_direction.title: Up or down
day1_pitch_direction.desc: Hear two notes, pick the direction
day1_pitch_direction.intro: A sound goes higher, lower, or stays where it is. Listen to two notes and only notice whether the second one sits above or below the first.
day1_pitch_direction.tip: Hum the two notes along. The direction becomes much clearer.

day2_long_short.title: Long and short
day2_long_short.intro: Music also speaks through length. Tell apart a sound that rings on, one that stops short, and a rest where nothing sounds.
day2_long_short.tip: Tap the table lightly while you listen and you'll feel the lengths in your body.

day3_leap.title: Near and far
day3_leap.desc: Feel the distance between two notes
day3_leap.intro: Notice how far apart two notes are. A close neighbor and a leap across town feel different. Once that's familiar we'll name them: thirds and fifths.
day3_leap.tip: A perfect fifth is the first two notes of 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star'.

day4_major_minor.title: Bright and dark
day4_major_minor.intro: The same tune feels bright and open in major and a little wistful in minor. Focus on the mood the sound gives you.
day4_major_minor.tip: When the third note dips slightly lower, the darker minor feeling appears.

day5_rhythm_pattern.title: Rhythm cards
day5_rhythm_pattern.intro: Now listen to a whole bar. Count the beats and match the order of long sounds, short sounds and rests to the card.
day5_rhythm_pattern.tip: Count 'one two three four' silently and the rests will show themselves.

day6_first_melody.title: First melody
day6_first_melody.intro: Hear a short melody that starts on do and pick the solfège. The first note is always do; just follow how far the next notes climb.
day6_first_melody.tip: Get 'do re mi' and 'do mi sol' into your mouth first and comparing gets easy.

day7_graduation.title: Final review
day7_graduation.intro: One question each on direction, length, distance, brightness, rhythm and melody from the past six days. Finish it and you graduate!
day7_graduation.tip: Mistakes are fine. Use 'Hear the answer' in the explanation to listen once more.

prompts.pitchDirection: Listen to two notes and pick where the second one went.
prompts.longShort: Listen to the length pattern and pick the matching one.
prompts.leapSize: Are the two notes close together or far apart?
prompts.leapName: Pick the distance between the two notes.
prompts.majorMinor: Listen to the short tune. Bright or dark?
prompts.rhythmPattern: Listen to the one-bar rhythm and pick the matching card.
prompts.firstMelody: Listen to the tune starting on do and pick the solfège.

direction.up: The second note was higher. When you sing along, a slight tightening in the throat means up.
direction.down: The second note was lower. Singing along, the sound settles down toward the chest.
direction.same: Both notes had the same pitch. No change means 'same'.

longShort.long_long: Two long sounds in a row, each ringing for two beats.
longShort.short_short_long: Two short sounds, then a long one that rings on at the end.
longShort.long_short_short: A long sound first, followed by two short ones.
longShort.sound_rest_sound_rest: Sound and rest alternated. The empty spot is the rest.
longShort.short_x4: Four even short sounds of the same length.

leapSize.near: The notes were only a couple of steps apart: a close leap that feels connected.
leapSize.wide: The notes were far apart: a wide leap that feels like a jump.

leapName.m3: A minor third: a small leap with a slightly dark, soft feel.
leapName.M3: A major third: a bright, open leap and the start of a major chord.
leapName.P5: A perfect fifth: wide and stable, like the first two notes of 'Twinkle, Twinkle'.

mode.major: It was major. The raised third note gives the bright, open feeling.
mode.minor: It was minor. The third note is a half step lower, which gives the wistful, darker feeling.

explain.rhythmPattern: Count 'one two three four' and match the order of long, short and rest to the card.
explain.firstMelody: The first note is always do. Follow how many steps each next note climbs and the solfège appears.
